item.title: Purdue basketball catches fires, burns Oakland with record performance
item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE − Finally, Purdue basketball buried an opponent after building a big lead. The Boilermakers' three-game winning streak saw buy game opponents Illinois State, Ohio and Lipscomb rally from double digits and make things too close for comfort after Valparaiso did the same and eventually upset Purdue in double overtime. Oakland failed to do what those teams could, quiet the typically raucous Mackey Arena fans. The Boilers built a 30-point halftime lead on their way to a 95-49 victory over the Grizzlies. And they did it in record-tying fashion. Purdue broke its program record with 21 made 3-pointers, passing a mark set at Iowa in 2018 . In the final minute, it was senior walk-on Jace Rayl who made the record breaker for his first career made field goal. Along the way, Purdue got some breakout performances for new pieces of the roster who are seemingly finding their fit. Purdue basketball turning point vs. Oakland Purdue's two losses to open the season can be blamed on many things, one of those its out of character atrociousness on 3-point attempts. During it's three-game winning streak, the Boilers shot 40.5% from beyond the arc. Gicarri Harris entered Friday's game making 10 of 18 3-pointers this season. Off the bench, the junior guard quickly buried 3s on consecutive possessions, putting Purdue ahead 15-4. It was a sign of things to come. Purdue sank 9 3-pointers in the first half at a 45% clip. Oakland couldn't recover from that blitz, which only got worse in the second half. Game MVP It was only a matter of time before Luke Ertel busted out. Last year's Indiana Mr. Basketball after leading Mt. Vernon to a Class 4A state championship caught fire against Oakland. Ertel drilled 8 of 10 3-pointers, finishing with a career-high 24 points. Ertel also showed his point guard mentality with 5 assists. More: Richard Moodie, bound for Tennessee, stays focused on Purdue soccer NCAA Tournament run Three Purdue basketball standouts vs. Oakland Jack Benter: Since being inserted into the starting lineup after those two losses to start the season, Benter has impressed. That was the case again against Oakland. Benter collected 9 points, 7 assists and 4 rebounds. Caden Pierce: Pierce, a former Ivy League Player of the Year at Princeton, has settled into his role as a starting power forward. Pierce can provide mismatches there and against Oakland that showed. Pierce had 13 points on 6 of 8 shooting. Daniel Jacobsen: The 7-foot-4 center continued his early season dominance. Jacobsen made 7 of 9 shots, scoring 16 points to go with 9 rebounds, 4 blocks and 2 assists. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. item.title: 'A great leader': Josh Hazlewood threatens Test exit if Cricket Australia sacks skipper Pat Cummins over Sandpapergate
item.description: 'A great leader': Josh Hazlewood threatens Test exit if Cricket Australia sacks skipper Pat Cummins over Sandpapergate originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Josh Hazlewood has publicly stood by Pat Cummins amid renewed ball-tampering claims from 2018. A dramatic hint about his own Test future has added heat to the row. The fast bowler explains what the bowlers did and didn’t see on the field. Josh Hazlewood denies Sandpapergate knowledge and warns of Test exit if Pat Cummins is removed as captain Josh Hazlewood described Pat Cummins as a "great leader" and the fast bowler has now backed those words with a show of loyalty as he has defended the Australian Test captain against fresh claims linked to the 2018 sandpaper scandal, also insisting that he knew nothing about any plan to alter the ball. Cummins has been under heavy fire since Usman Khawaja said the entire team was aware of the plot during the Cape Town Test of 2018. David Warner and, more recently, Cameron Bancroft have made similar claims that everyone in the group knew about the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball. Hazlewood has sided with Cummins, who has always said he took no part in the plan. The 35-year-old has taken 313 Test wickets, and in 2021 he co-signed a document along with Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, in which all four denied any prior knowledge of sandpaper being taken onto the field. Hazlewood described the criticism of his captain since Bancroft’s 4,000-word column earlier this week as “a bit of a pile on”. He then told Code Sports that he believes the work Cummins has done with the group is remarkable, and that the team is now in a place where such an incident would never be repeated. “To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that (sandpaper) is never going to happen again – I think is just a remarkable job," he said. item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 42 - Kevin Willis (1996-98, 2001-02)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the eighth of 12 who wore the No. 42, Kevin Willis. After ending his college career at Michigan State, Willis was picked up with the 11th overall selection of the 1984 NBA Draft by the Atlanta Hawks. The Los Angeles, California native played the first 10 seasons of his pro career with Atlanta. He also played for the Miami Heat and Golden State Warriors before he joined the Houston Rockets for the first time in free agency in 1996. It ended with a trade to the Toronto Raptors in 1998. Between stints, he played for the Denver Nuggets and Milwaukee Bucks before he was dealt back to Houston in 2001, lasting until he signed with the San Antonio Spurs in 2002. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Willis wore only jersey No. 42 and put up 11.8 points and 7.4 rebounds per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: LeBron James has Sixers drawing 215,000 viewers in Philadelphia market
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images LeBron James is big business, and that fact is paying off for the Philadelphia 76ers. On the court, the Sixers are off to a 13–2 start to the season — their best since 2000 — and current stand atop the Eastern Conference. But beyond their record, James’s impact on all of the business that surrounds the team may be even greater. A report from Rob Tornoe at the Philadelphia Inquirer noted that the Sixers are drawing in 215,000 viewers in the Philadelphia area per game this year on NBC Sports Philadelphia, which owns the local broadcast rights for the team. It’s a 150% increase over last season. The impact of James has been so great that it is even shaking up the local news scene in Philadelphia. According to Tonroe, while Action News at 6ABC is still the top news program in the area, NBC10 is presenting the “first serious ratings challenge” to their spot in years with help from the bump the Sixers have provided. NBC10 president and general manager Joel Davis noted that the network’s cross-promotion between its news desk and its sports team covering the Sixers has been a boon to expanding their reach. “When we run news promos in NBC Sports Philadelphia, we are getting a younger audience exposed to our news product,” Davis told Tornoe. While whatever boost LeBron provides to the team can only last as long as he keeps playing, there’s reason to believe the Sixers are set to only grow in their share of ratings from here. Usually, this part of the calendar would be mostly reserved for the Eagles in the greater Philadelphia area, but with the Birds playing like one of the worst teams in the NFL, the Sixers have been able to stake their claim on the local sports scene a bit earlier than usual. If the wins keep coming and they look like they can make a real run through the postseason, it’s possible we’re only seeing the very beginning of what the LeBron effect looks like in full. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Golden State Warriors - Tony Farmer
item.description: The Golden State Warriors have signed, drafted, and traded for players from nearly every U.S. state and many countries around the world. From Alaska to Wyoming and Austria to Zaire, the Warriors have a strong history of seeking out talent necessary for NBA success. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor to the NBA) when they got their start as the team representing Philadelphia before they made their move to the West Coast, the organization has consistently pursued talent from a broad range of sources. For this installment of our series taking stock of the birthplace of every Golden State player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for the Warriors. Our focus in this article is Tony Farmer. An alum of Nebraska, he went unselected in the 1991 NBA Draft, playing in other leagues until he signed with the Charlotte Hornets in 1997. The Los Angeles, California native played the first season of his NBA career with Charlotte, returning to other leagues until he signed with the Dubs in 1999 for his final campaign in the league. During his time suiting up for the Warriors, Farmer put up 6.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.1 assists per game. All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference. item.title: Yankees Flagged as Potential ‘Mystery’ Team in Tarik Skubal Rumors
item.description: Tarik Skubal instagram story Getty The New York Yankees could be embarking on a quiet campaign to land top free agent prize Tarik Skubal. The star pitcher has garnered interest from several teams — and a reported $400 million offer from the crosstown New York Mets — but the Yankees have not been publicly identified yet as one of them. But one MLB insider believes the Bronx Bombers could be the still-unnamed “mystery” team that has reportedly met with Skubal this week. Yankees Could Be Pursuing Tarik Skubal MLB.com reported that Skubal has already held several on-the-books meetings with teams, along with one more secretive visit. “We know that Skubal has reportedly held meetings with the Mets, the Blue Jays, the Dodgers and the Padres this week. But there is at least one other team in the mix; we just don’t know which one,” the report noted. “MLB Network insider Jon Heyman reports in the New York Post ( subscription required ) that a fifth team met over Zoom with Skubal on Wednesday. Which team? That is undisclosed, per Heyman. But it’s possible that club and the ace left-hander could have an in-person meeting later.” While there are still no solid reports on the identity of that “mystery team” pursuing Skubal, SI.com writer Noah Camras suggested it would only be logical that the Yankees are in the mix. “The Yankees don’t need starting pitching, but have the financial muscle to sign Skubal if they wanted to,” Camras wrote. “Big-name free agents always love to have as many big-market teams pursuing them as possible. Thus, why wouldn’t the Yankees at the very least be in the running?” The Yankees have gone toe-to-toe with the Mets when chasing free agents before, losing out on Juan Soto to New York’s $765 million offer. But Camras suggested that a more logical team could be Skubal’s unnamed suitor, noting that the Detroit Tigers are open to a return, as is Skubal. Yankees Could Focus on Other Roster Needs The Yankees have already made some big moves to boost their pitching staff. Closer David Bednar accepted this one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, while Tim Hill returned on a new one-year deal. With the moves to boost the bullpen, some insiders expect the Yankees to focus on finding a second baseman to replace Jazz Chisholm, as well as some other moves for their infield. item.title: Verstappen and Russell at war as explosive FP3 incident sparks FIA investigation
item.description: Max Verstappen and George Russell were involved in a heated confrontation during the closing stages of the third free practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , with the two drivers making contact before the Dutchman showed his middle finger to the Mercedes driver. The incident will be investigated by the stewards after the session. The confrontation began when Verstappen overtook Russell along the Las Vegas Strip, positioning his Red Bull directly ahead of the Mercedes before beginning to weave from side to side as the two approached the braking zone. Russell responded aggressively, diving down the inside under braking in an attempt to reclaim the position. The two drivers came extremely close together and eventually made contact as the Mercedes driver forced his way back ahead. However, the confrontation did not end there. Shortly afterwards, Verstappen moved back in front of Russell and made his frustration clear by showing the British driver his middle finger. Race control subsequently noted the incident, with the stewards confirming that the encounter between the two drivers would be investigated after FP3. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen's frustrations boil over after difficult session The confrontation came at the end of an already frustrating session for the four-time world champion, who repeatedly struggled under braking throughout the hour. Despite setting the pace during the opening stages, Verstappen complained that his Red Bull felt too "sharp" and subsequently made several mistakes, running wide on at least four occasions and being forced to turn around before continuing. The incident with Russell was also the second time Verstappen attracted the attention of the stewards during FP3. Earlier in the session, the Dutchman had been involved in a potentially dangerous encounter with Franco Colapinto while weaving to warm his tyres. The Argentine approached from behind before overtaking Verstappen on the start-finish straight, only for the Red Bull driver to reclaim the position at Turn 1. That incident was also referred to the stewards for a post-session investigation. Meanwhile, Russell went on to dominate the session with a remarkable 1:34.041, finishing almost a second ahead of Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli. Verstappen eventually finished sixth, 1.309 seconds behind Russell, with two separate stewards' investigations awaiting him after the chequered flag.

item.title: University of New Haven football found a Connecticut 'hidden gem' in Valley Regional receiver Tommy Troy
item.description: Tommy Troy, a sophomore from Essex who played at Valley Regional, is one the University of New Haven's top receivers with 19 catches for 269 yards and three touchdowns. (Photo courtesy of UNH Athletics) NEW BRITAIN - The first time Tommy Troy stepped onto the University of New Haven campus, the thoughts of suiting up for a perennial Division II playoff team was rather appealing. Things can change in the college football world and a little over a month before Troy graduated from Valley Regional High School, the university where he would head for the next stage of his football career announced the move to Division I. It seemed like a match made in heaven for the talented receiver. Mark Powell, the new head coach of the Chargers, was looking for some new faces to help make the move up in class and was hoping to land some talented home-grown players to build around. Troy was exactly the type of player Powell was trying to find. The sophomore from Essex is one the Chargers top receivers with 19 catches for 269 yards and three touchdowns. At 6-foot-3, he is always an option in the red zone as he is the only New Haven player with more than one touchdown catch this season. "I think there are a lot of underrecruited kids in Connecticut, I came from a Class S school," Troy said after making three catches in a 42-20 loss to two-time defending Northeast Conference champion Central Connecticut State. "I think there are a lot of hidden gems around here and I want to do everything I can for my team, whether it is blocking or catching passes." Eight Connecticut natives got onto the field for the Chargers against CCSU. Woodstock's Lucas Theriaque had an interception, Windsor's Chris Hudson made three tackles, and New Haven's Frank Daniley carried the ball five times and also had a reception. Powell can point to those players, as well as Troy as players who opted to stay home and are helping the Chargers make the challenging jump to playing at the Football Championship Subdivision level. "Tommy's done an awesome job. It is awesome for me, being from and playing at Notre Dame-West Haven and watching a kid from Valley come up and do it," Powell said. "It is really, really awesome to see what he has done and he continues to grow every single week. He's going to continue to get better and better. I think his ceiling is extremely high. "I do think Connecticut gets underrecruited. There is a lot of really good talent, you just have to work at it. We have to look at it from a holistic standpoint, the level of competition and all the rest of it, I understand. There are a lot of really good football players in the state and Tommy Troy is one of them. He has done a great job for us. We are going to continue to try to find the Tommy Troys, the Frank Danileys, the local kids and we are going to continue to build this thing with local talent." item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Bears are getting several important players back for Sunday’s game against the Saints. They just won’t emerge from the bye with every injury question resolved. Kyle Monangai, Malik Muhammad II, Luther Burden III and Jeffery Simmons all practiced fully Friday and carry no game designation. Monangai is expected to return after missing five games, while Muhammad is set to rejoin the secondary following a two-game absence. But Kyler Gordon has been ruled out with a shoulder injury, and rookie receiver and kickoff returner Zavion Thomas is questionable after an ankle issue kept him out of Friday’s practice. It leaves Chicago with reinforcements on both sides of the ball and decisions to make before kickoff at Soldier Field. item.title: Is Lightning’s Success Giving Nikita Kucherov a Reason to Reconsider?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tampa Bay Lightning have spent much of November looking like a team capable of making another serious run at the Stanley Cup but whether that is enough to convince Nikita Kucherov to reconsider his future with the organization remains a much more complicated question. Kucherov publicly confirmed earlier this month that he had requested a trade and did not intend to sign a new contract with the Lightning, citing communication and respect rather than money as the reasons behind his decision. The 33-year-old is in the final season of his eight-year, $76 million contract and could become the most coveted unrestricted free agent next July 1. General manager Julien BriseBois has publicly maintained that the Lightning have no intention of trading their franchise winger. In the meantime, Kucherov has continued producing at an elite level, and the team around him is giving him plenty of reasons to believe it can still compete. Between Nov. 5 and Nov. 19, the Lightning outscored their opponents 19-9 at five-on-five across seven games, according to a comparison of MoneyPuck’s season-to-date data. That plus-10 goal differential was tied for the second-best mark in the NHL over the same window. Kucherov was at the center of that success. The Russian winger scored five goals across all situations during the 14-day stretch, generating 3.06 individual expected goals. At five-on-five, he scored three times on 2.02 expected goals, ranking among the league leaders in both categories. Perhaps more impressive was what happened when he was on the ice. The Lightning outscored opponents 11-3 during Kucherov’s five-on-five minutes, giving him one of the league’s strongest on-ice scoring differentials over the two-week period. And he wasn’t the only Lightning forward putting together an impressive stretch. Lightning’s stars are producing together Brandon Hagel has been one of the NHL’s most productive forwards in recent weeks. Across five games in the comparison window, he scored five goals at five-on-five while generating 2.81 individual expected goals, the highest total in the league. The Lightning outscored opponents 8-1 with Hagel on the ice at five-on-five. Jake Guentzel has been similarly effective. item.description: Maple Leafs Jim Hiller Getty Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller offered some blunt comments on his job security after reports that he could be fired emerged. The Maple Leafs have lost eight games in a row, and Hiller has come under fire for some questionable decisions with the team’s lineup, including not playing No. 1 overall pick Gavin McKenna in 3-on-3 overtime during the team’s loss to the Los Angeles Kings on Thursday night. That’s why fans want to see the team make a change, even though Maple Leafs GM John Chayka recently gave Hiller a vote of confidence. Therefore, making a change behind the bench would be something that would be a major disappointment for the club, given they are only 24 games into the Hiller era, but it would also be understandable given how bad the team has looked this season. Jim Hiller Admits the Pressure is Boiling Up Toronto is one of the toughest markets to play hockey in, both for players and for coaches. item.description: Simon Edvinsson of the Detroit Red Wings. Getty The Simon Edvinsson situation could finally be getting close to a resolution. The end of the saga will be a trade with a still-unknown party at this time. That’s the latest on the situation, according to insider David Pagnotta. According to an article in the Fourth Period, Pagnotta discussed how the Edvinsson situation could be nearing a conclusion, particularly with the December 1 deadline looming around the corner. “Trade discussions involving Detroit Red Wings restricted free agent Simon Edvinsson have picked up steam and have reached a point where the young star defenceman is preparing for a move, according to sources.” The chatter makes sense as there was really no way that the Red Wings were going to be able to re-sign the 23-year-old blueliner. The talk had focused on the fact that Simon Edvinsson did not want to return to Detroit, and was even willing to go back to Sweden if a trade could not happen before December 1. Pagnotta did confirm that two Western Conference clubs were reportedly close on the situation, among six total teams. “Red Wings GM Shawn Horcoff continues to navigate trade negotiations, with it confirmed to me that the Nashville Predators and San Jose Sharks are among at least six clubs still in pursuit of the first-pair blueliner.” At this point, there is no firm timeline. However, the idea is that a deal could happen at some point in the middle of next week, ideally a few days before the December 1 deadline. If Simon Edvinsson does not sign by then, he would become ineligible to play this season. Red Wings Could Unlock Dylan Larkin Situation with Simon Edvinsson Trade The belief around the league is that a Simon Edvinsson trade would unlock the Dylan Larkin situation. The idea hinges on Detroit being able to get a piece or pieces that would change the equation on Larkin. For instance, the thought is that the Red Wings want a center to replace Larkin in their lineup. They’re not getting that from Larkin’s approved list. Nevertheless, Detroit may get it from another team in an Edvinsson deal. If that’s the case, the Red Wings can then get the piece they need and potentially take a different sort of deal for Larkin. The Clock Is Ticking As mentioned earlier, the clock is ticking. Edvinsson remains an RFA and can legally talk to any team. Unfortunately, the Red Wings hold his rights, keeping him from signing a contract with any team. That’s why a trade has to happen. And because a trade has to happen, the clock is ticking unless Edvinsson is willing to sign a deal just to keep his season alive. item.title: F1 Las Vegas GP: George Russell tops final practice after Max Verstappen collision
item.description: Motorsport photo George Russell collided with Max Verstappen in a tense third practice session at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as the Mercedes Formula 1 driver topped the timesheets. After both of Thursday's practice sessions had been derailed by rain, the Las Vegas Strip was buzzing with activity at dusk on Friday. The sole remaining practice session became crucial as it presented the only dry running heading into qualifying and the race, as all 22 cars sprinted out of the pitlane in short order. Amid chilly 14C temperatures, the Thursday rainfall only made the 6.2km circuit around the Las Vegas Strip even more difficult to drive, with surface grip extremely limited. Verstappen survived a sideways scare and steering rack issues to lead the early running with a 1m35.675s on soft tyres, by far the most popular tyre in cold conditions as it was easier to fire up to temperature. Just after the halfway mark Russell took over top spot with a 1m35.124s, the Briton aiming to finish the season on a high as he declined a Mercedes turbo upgrade to avoid a grid penalty. Russell further lowered his own benchmark to a 1m34.805s lap, before becoming one of several cars to find the runoff area on the slippery circuit. The urgency to get plenty of clean laps in was on full display with Verstappen and Franco Colapinto almost coming to blows in their quest for clean air. Verstappen's Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar also lobbied for a penalty for Williams' Alex Albon. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Annoyed by Verstappen forcing his way past, Lando Norris couldn't hide his glee when the four-time world champion subsequently locked up and sailed into the runoff area. "Instant karma, amazing," he said over team radio. The biggest clash followed right at the end of the session, again involving Verstappen, as he tried a similar move on Russell on the straight. Undeterred, Russell sent his Mercedes down the inside of Turn 14 to re-pass the Red Bull, making side-on contact as he muscled Verstappen off the track. The incident will be investigated by the FIA’s stewards. "Fun and games," Russell described the incident on the radio. Norris initially came closest to overhauling Russell in the closing minutes of the session, settling for second with a 1m35.060s lap. Russell found late improvements too, though, to pull out a massive seven-tenth lead on Norris at the top of the timesheets with laps of 1m34.306s and 1m34.041s. item.title: ‘Drives me bonkers all the technology and AI': Charley Hull is logging off
item.description: Charley Hull tees off on Friday on the 4th hole. Getty Images Charley Hull, to be clear, will still have a phone. But only a phone. You can call her. She may call you. End of conversation. “Yeah, just an old-school phone,” Hull said. Which means no apps. No social media. No photos. No videos. This week, the world’s eighth-ranked player is playing the CME Group Tour Championship, the LPGA’s season-ender, and 2026, she said Thursday, has felt never-ending. Tournaments. Solheim Cup . Various appearances. There is also WTGL , the simulator-based league that started just a few weeks ago. But when her play is finished there, Hull said she is powering down. Literally. And she can’t wait. “After WTGL I’m going to go home,” Hull said, “I’m going to buy myself a Nokia phone and for the whole month just change my sim over and just have a Nokia phone and just completely switch off from the world.” What does that look like? “Yeah, just an old-school phone so I can’t look at anything,” the Englishwoman said. “Don’t have to worry about anything. If anyone wants to get hold of me, call me on that phone. Like I’m done with texting, I’m done with social media. “I just want to have a whole month detox.” Should you be heavily connected to your phone — there’s probably a good chance you’re reading this article on your cell — you may know what Hull is feeling. Going off the grid, she said, is therapeutic. She’s done it previously. In 2019, she said she went four months without a phone — and she was in Asia. She did have an iPad, and a companion had her flight info. How did she feel when that was over? “Oh, so much better,” Hull said. “Honestly, I wish I was born 30, 40 years earlier because I just — drives me bonkers all the technology and AI these days.” In her session with reporters on Thursday, Hull also shared another “detox” story. That one came from her win a decade ago at the Tour Championship. She’d been asked how she would compare her game then to what it looks like now, and she said this: “It’s so funny. Back when I won 10 years ago, I didn’t really take golf seriously. I remember coming into this event 10 years ago, when I won, like, hungover. I was out Thursday, Friday, Saturday drinking with my friends and stuff. “My mom and dad was fuming when I come back Saturday. Dad was like, ‘So bad with what you done as preparation. You’re meant to be a professional athlete. You’re going to miss the cut this week.’ I turned around to him and I was like, ‘Dad, there is no cut, so ha.’ “Anyway, I got to the hotel room and messaged my friends and I was like, I feel like I’m in a massive detox this week. “So like the hotel rooms here, have my Netflix on the TV, just completely detox from all the alcohol that I drank, and then end up winning. “So, yeah, it was pretty crazy.” The post ‘Drives me bonkers all the technology and AI': Charley Hull is logging off appeared first on Golf .
